newsitem.title: USA: Peru can now focus on important economic issues.
newsitem.headline: Peru can now focus on important economic issues.

text.p: The dramatic end to the Peruvian hostage crisis will allow the government to focus on important economic issues that had been put largely on hold since the 126-day siege began, Latin experts said Wednesday.

"I think the important idea now is that government is not distracted by the crisis and can focus on the more salient economic issues that have been on the back burner for a while," said Marco Santamaria, emerging market fixed-income analyst at ING Barings in New York.
The hostage crisis ended Tuesday when President Alberto Fujimori ordered Peruvian troops to storm the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
The raid freed 71 hostages but resulted in the deaths of one hostage, two soldiers and all the 14 Tupac Amaru (MRTA) rebels.
Experts said the Peruvian government can move ahead with key structural reforms such as privatisations and the reform of the state now that the crisis has ended.

"All of those issues that have not been tackled during this hostage period may now come in the limelight again as the government turns its attention to these things, and to that extent, it may encourage foreign direct and portfolio investors to have a rosier view of the likely evolution of Peru," Santamaria said.

"Now that the crisis is over, we should see a little more focus on the privatisation programme and a little more comfort level among foreign investors," added William Romary, senior Latin economist at UBS Securities in New York.
"Those on the margin who had been holding back not sure if they wanted to make a commitment may be more inclined to do so," he said.
Latin experts also said Fujimori's decision to storm the aassador's residence and the favourable outcome should certainly have a positive effect on investor sentiment.

"It was a big gamble for Fujimori but it paid off. The outcome certainly is a positive and I think it will be positive for (both foreign direct and portfolio) investment flows into Peru," said Romary.
Indeed, Peruvian debt prices surged Tuesday following the the release of the hostages but the market saw some slight profit-taking today following the sharp gains.
